newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks leap ahead of CANTV offer.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks leap ahead of CANTV offer.

text.p: Caracas stocks leapt ahead in high volume as investors refocused their attention on Venezuelan equities ahead of Friday's placement of 50 million shares in telephone company CANTV on the bolsa, traders said.
"This could be the start of the rally the market's been waiting for ever since the CANTV placement began," said Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi.
The CANTV placement is expected to draw foreign funds to the market boosting other stocks. The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index gained 1.87 percent to close at 6,164.86 points.
The stock issue is also seen as an important test of the government's commitment to economic reforms.

Among traded issues, 28 rose, ten fell and 13 closed flat. A total of 102 million shares exchanged hands, boosted by a cross trade of 86 million shares in insurer General de Seguros, worth 8.5 billion bolivars ($18 million).
"Discounting the Seguros trade, if these levels of trade volume continue there's definitely room for something of a market rally," said Isasi.

Among widely held stocks Electricidad de Caracas gained 9.50 bolivars to close at 549.50, steel company Sivensa moved ahead 5.55 bolivars to end at 360.00 while foods company Mavesa dropped 1.00 bolivar to end at 150.00.
